newsitem.title: UK: British 1997/98 sugar beet sowings race ahead.
newsitem.headline: British 1997/98 sugar beet sowings race ahead.

text.p: Britain is racing ahead with sowings for the 1997/98 sugar beet crop, an official at British Sugar said on Tuesday.
As of last weekend 68 percent of the crop was already in ground, compared with 30 percent at the same stage last year, the official said.

"The word is that this is probably a record figure for this time of the year. They (farmers) are within the drilling window of March 10 to April 10," he said, noting that some frost was forecast for the coming weekend.
Britain is expected to have a total beet area of 170,000 hectares, the same as in 1996/97.
Beet planting trials were held earlier this month.

Britain produced a record 1.48 million tonnes of sugar in white value terms from its 1996/97 beet crop. The previous record was in 1992/93, when around 1,000 tonnes less sugar was produced. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
